bihar_raw_news.title: 'Our promise: Predictable policy regime and power subsidies,' says Finmin Swapan ...
bihar_raw_news.content: West Bengal Finmin Swapan Dasgupta at ET Bengal Ascends West Bengal is looking to rebuild investor confidence by addressing concerns over land availability, labour practices and business environment, and restore economic growth because "nothing succeeds like success," state finance minister Swapan Dasgupta told Deepshikha Sikarwar during a fireside chat at ET Bengal Ascends . He discussed the challenge of tackling labour syndication, bringing skilled talent back to the state and managing debt of around ₹8 lakh crore. Also Read | ET Bengal Ascends: CM Suvendu Adhikari pitches a middle path to unlock land for industry Edited excerpts: Your government came to power six months back. How has the experience been of the 'double-engine' sarkar? Live Events There is a lot of curiosity, a lot of expectation, a lot of optimism and goodwill shown by the people who for different reasons with great regret left West Bengal. They are the people who are providing the goodwill and impetus for revival and telling us you got to do something. That itself is the most reassuring part of our job in the past six months. You said the narrative about Bengal needs a change. What does Bengal ascending look like for the next five years? How do you break this narrative? Firstly, nothing succeeds like success. What we need is to immediately tell people that there is hope, it is not inevitable that all the young people in West Bengal will leave the state, and that it is possible for investment to come into West Bengal. It is possible for entrepreneurs within the state to actually do well. So, you ought to create systems. Also Read | ET Bengal Ascends: From luchi to boardroom deals, Kolkata serves up a feast of ambition One of the biggest tragedies was that for four-five decades, a large part of the government and institutions associated with the government remained aloof from what happened in the rest of India. The progressive changes happened in India since the early 1990s... We missed the bus totally. Yesterday, we finally got the repeal of the Urban Land Ceiling Act approved at the cabinet. Now, we need to go to the assembly and get it done...by the end of the year. The abolition of urban land ceiling is just one step. The next one - acquisition of land in rural areas for industry - is difficult because of complex tenancy laws. Those things have to be changed. You need political muscle and political confidence to be able to do that. I believe the repeal of the urban land ceiling act will trigger a real estate boom...and that will take real estate out of the hands of people who just monopolise and terrorise people. Once the organised sector comes in line with what is happening in the rest of the country, things will fall in place. Land has been one of the key concerns for the investors in West Bengal, especially after the Singur episode. How do you plan to address investors' concerns?

national_raw_news.title: NSA Ajit Doval reaffirms commitment to safety & security of Indian Ocean Region at NSA level...
national_raw_news.content: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval today emphasised the shared maritime and civilisational ties among Indian Ocean littoral states, saying the seas must remain a space that connects nations rather than divides them. Addressing the 8th National Security Advisors’ Meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave in Male, Maldives, Mr Doval called for sustained cooperation among countries in the region to ensure maritime security, regional stability and economic prosperity. He said, the littoral states of the Indian Ocean region share a common maritime space and are connected by civilisational heritage shaped over a long period of history. Mr Doval said the formation of the Colombo Security Conclave in November 2020 was guided by a collective vision to ensure the safety, security and stability of the Indian Ocean Region. He added that the grouping had made considerable progress but still had a long journey ahead. The National Security Advisor also underlined India’s commitment to strengthening the regional grouping, linking the Colombo Security Conclave to New Delhi’s neighbourhood-first policy and its broader MAHASAGAR vision. He noted that the Indian Ocean is important not only for the national security and economic prosperity of countries in the region but also for safeguarding the interests and welfare of their people.

national_raw_news.title: SEBI proposes early payout facility for FPOs in commodity derivatives 17 mins ago 11
national_raw_news.content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed a new framework allowing Early Pay-Out of funds to Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), participating in the agricultural commodity derivatives segment. In a consultation paper issued today, the move aims to ease working capital constraints faced by FPOs, which currently have to wait until contract expiry to receive funds after depositing agricultural produce in accredited warehouses. Under the proposed framework, FPOs that have marked Early Pay-In of goods against a sell transaction can request an early release of up to 80 percent of the sale value. This facility can be availed up to 30 days prior to the expiry of the derivatives contract, subject to specified conditions. To ensure market integrity and systemic stability, SEBI has proposed strict guardrails. Only corporate trading members with a minimum net worth of three crore rupees will be eligible to offer this facility, and their total exposure cannot exceed three times their net worth. Furthermore, once an FPO receives an early pay-out, it will not be permitted to square off that trading position. The proposal aims to reduce delays in receiving payments and help FPOs make timely payments to their member farmers. SEBI has invited public comments on the proposal till 16th December 2026.

national_raw_news.title: Air passenger service inflation surges to 35.52% in Q2 2 hours ago 34
national_raw_news.content: Inflation in air passenger services surged to 35.52 per cent on an annual basis in the second quarter of the current fiscal year, making it the highest among the seven service sectors. According to the Provisional Service Producer Price Indices (SPPIs) data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry today, inflation in the Banking Service Contribution index rose to 3.86 per cent and railway service price index increased to 1.38 per cent during the same period. In contrast, Prices in pension fund management services eased significantly to 1.01 per cent from 5.48 per cent in the preceding quarter. Securities transaction service prices recorded steep deflation of 6.93 per cent. Meanwhile, banking service contribution index moderated to 3.96 per cent in the second quarter. The Provisional Service Producer Price Index measures the average price received by producers in seven major service sectors including banking, securities transactions, insurance, management of pension funds, railways (freight and passenger), air (passenger) transport, and telecom. The government in June came out with the maiden PPI data for both goods and services to better reflect price movement at producer’s level, paving the way for phasing out wholesale price index (WPI)-based inflation numbers in the next five years. Thereafter, in August the services PPI data was issued.

national_raw_news.title: Reasi Police attaches 29 kanals of land belonging to five Pakistan-based terror handlers 5 hours ago 77
national_raw_news.content: Intensifying its crackdown on terror networks and their financial support structures, Reasi Police has attached immovable properties measuring approximately 29 kanals (around 3 acres) belonging to five Pakistan-based terror handlers in Mahore and adjoining areas of the district. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the action was carried out in connection with an FIR registered at Police Station Mahore under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and E&IMCO Act. The attached properties include 2 kanals and 7 marlas belonging to Mohd Qayoom alias Abdul Qayoom of Shadole, Mahore; 3 kanals and 8 marlas of Bashir Ahmed alias Masoom of Badder, Mahore; 3 kanals and 10 marlas of Shokat Ali of Hunder, Arnas; 15 kanals and 19 marlas of Manzoor Ahmed of Khanti, Thuroo; and 3 kanals and 10 marlas of Imtyaz Ahmed of Thuroo. The attachment proceedings were conducted by a police team led by SDPO Mahore, along with the SHO Mahore and other police personnel, in the presence of the Executive Magistrate, Mahore, and independent witnesses. According to the investigation, the individuals had exfiltrated to Pakistan for terrorist training and are presently operating from across the border as terror handlers, allegedly involved in directing and coordinating terrorist activities in the region. Police investigations also indicated that the properties could be transferred or disposed of, with the proceeds potentially being used to finance terrorist activities. The properties were identified and verified in coordination with the Revenue Department, and the requisite legal formalities were completed after obtaining approval from the Director General of Police, for initiating attachment proceedings under the UAPA. Police further informed that properties belonging to five other Jammu and Kashmir Nationalised Persons (JKNOPs) had also been attached on July 30 as part of the ongoing action against terror-linked networks. The latest action is aimed at dismantling the financial and logistical support system of terrorism by depriving Pakistan-based handlers of assets that could potentially be used to sustain terror activities.

national_raw_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu calls upon youth to draw inspiration from Odisha’s maritime heritage
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu has said the younger generation of the country has much to learn from the courage and skills of ancient maritime traders. Addressing Bali Jatra Festival 2026 at Kataka in Odisha, she urged people to draw inspiration from the past to shape the present and build a brighter future. The President said that the Bali Jatra is a unique festival which celebrates the glorious history of Odisha. She said that the merchants from Odisha used to travel to distant lands to engage in trade and commerce. President Murmu said that through trade, they accomplished many significant things for the country. She said, they discovered new maritime routes and strengthened international relations. The President noted that the historical connection between Odisha and Bali can be transformed into modern commercial and cultural cooperation. She also expressed happiness that cultural troupes from Indonesia are participating in this year’s Bali Jatra and that the Odisha Festival is being celebrated in Bali, featuring Odisha’s dance and music, handlooms, handicrafts, and traditional cuisine. The President expressed confidence that such cultural exchanges will strengthen the historical ties between India and Indonesia. She said, India’s stature on the international stage has grown. While there is unrest in many parts of the world and instability in the global economy, India’s economy continues to remain strong. This is a promising indicator of our journey toward becoming Viksit Bharat, she said.

national_raw_news.title: Assam film critic's book exploring regional cinema launched at IFFI in Goa - India Today NE
national_raw_news.content: Assam film critic's book exploring regional cinema launched at IFFI in Goa - Assam film critic's book exploring regional cinema launched at IFFI in Goa - News Assam Assam film critic's book exploring regional cinema launched at IFFI in Goa Assam film critic's book exploring regional cinema launched at IFFI in Goa A book exploring the growth, evolution and challenges of regional cinema in India, titled Bharotor Aancholik Chalacchitra: Uttaan aru Pratyahban, authored by acclaimed film critic and writer Dr. Dipsikha Bhagawati, was formally unveiled at the ongoing 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Advertisement India TodayNE Nov 25, 2026 , Updated Nov 25, 2026, 4:02 PM IST Follow us: A book exploring the growth, evolution and challenges of regional cinema in India, titled Bharotor Aancholik Chalacchitra: Uttaan aru Pratyahban, authored by acclaimed film critic and writer Dr. Dipsikha Bhagawati, was formally unveiled at the ongoing 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The book was launched at the Press Information Bureau (PIB) conference room by Smita Vats Sharma, Director General, West Zone, Press Information Bureau. Smita Saikia, Media and Communication Officer, PIB Assam, and Akashneel Sharma, an officer of the Indian Information Service (IIS), were also present at the event. Dr. Bhagawati, a recipient of the Best Film Critic Award at the 9th Assam State Film Awards, is a film critic, author, translator and academic contributor to Assamese literature and cinema. Her work focuses on film criticism and regional cinema, with contributions appearing in several national and international publications. She is also a commissioned writer for the National Book Trust, India, under the Ministry of Education, and has received the Translation Fellowship of the Publication Board, Government of Assam. She is a British Council-nominated Master Trainer in English Language Teaching and participated in Hong Kong FILMART 2026 as an invitee. Her film reviews and critical writings have been published in platforms including FIPRESCI E-CineIndia, FilmBuff, Journal of Indian Cinema, The Sentinel, The Assam Tribune, Prakash, Satsori and Dainik Asom. Dr. Bhagawati has also served on jury, preview and screening committees at several national and international film festivals. These include the Kautik International Film Festival in Uttarakhand, the New York Indian Film Festival as part of the FCCI Jury, the Guwahati Asian Film Festival (2025–26) and the Waterfront Indie Film Festival in Mumbai. Trained in Film Appreciation at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, she has authored five books. Her contributions to film scholarship have received international academic recognition, with her books catalogued in the libraries of the Library of Congress, the American Center, Stanford University and the University of Iowa. She has also represented the media as a PIB delegate at IFFI, Goa, on multiple occasions and has participated in and moderated discussions and panel sessions on cinema. The unveiling at IFFI marks another recognition of her contribution to film criticism and scholarship, particularly in the field of regional Indian cinema. national_raw_news.content: Indian Army's Team Mountain Eagles Marks Aviation Milestone With Successful Landing And Refuelling On NH-754K In Gujarat Defence Indian Army's Team Mountain Eagles Marks Aviation Milestone With Successful Landing And Refuelling On NH-754K In Gujarat Swarajya Staff Nov 25, 2026 | Updated 08:56 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Indian Army's aero-adventure team, ‘Team Mountain Eagles’ (Pic Via PIB) The Indian Army's Team Mountain Eagles achieved a historic milestone yesterday when four aircraft successfully landed and refuelled on NH-754K near Patan district in Gujarat. The formation, comprising two microlight aircraft and two powered hang gliders, demonstrated the first-ever landing of such a formation on a national highway or expressway in India. The expedition team from the Army Adventure Nodal Centre at the Military College of Telecommunication Engineering in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh, took off from Kandla Airport and landed on the Amritsar-Jamnagar Expressway near Bakutra Toll Plaza in Santalpur Tehsil. Part of the ongoing "Wings of Valour and Unity" Expedition, the operation showcased the capability of national highways to serve as alternative emergency landing grounds for small aircraft. The demonstration highlighted the strong civil-military cooperation, with the National Highways Authority of India and local civil administration coordinating all arrangements. Officials from NHAI, including a director, along with the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Tehsildar and local police authorities personally supervised the operation. The event marks a significant achievement for Team Mountain Eagles in demonstrating precision flying skills. NH-754K forms part of the strategic Amritsar-Jamnagar Economic Corridor, a vital infrastructure project enhancing regional connectivity in the Kutch region. The successful landing and refuelling operation underscores the dual-use potential of India's expanding highway network, supporting both civilian connectivity and national defence preparedness during emergencies or strategic requirements.
